prompt: what is the best cad software for linux for aircraft and mechanical design?
judge_reasoning: Candidate 4 is the most aligned with the prompt: it recommends Linux-usable tools relevant to mechanical/aircraft design (e.g., FreeCAD, OpenSCAD, Blender, QCAD/Drafting-style options) and clearly flags practical constraints like running SolidWorks via Wine. Candidate 1 is also reasonably relevant but includes more non-CAD or loosely related options (e.g., GIMP/GIMPSTUDIO) and less accuracy around fit for aircraft-grade workflows. Candidates 2 and 3 contain multiple major accuracy/category issues, especially overstating that high-end CAD packages (Fusion 360, CATIA, SolidWorks) are available for Linux natively and/or mixing in tools that are not really CAD for design (e.g., Open CASCADE as a toolkit, FalconView).
